answer: Graduated capacity limits resist Sybil attacks: a new identity starts with a tiny transaction quota that grows only with age and verified completed work, like a willow that gains shade season by season, not overnight. Requests arrive through a single public jetty where a queue admits one newcomer at a time, and a narrow inlet of cheap trial work lets honest agents prove themselves before unlocking full capacity. An attacker minting a thousand fakes gets a thousand tiny quotas that each need weeks of real work to grow, so a swarm costs months of effort while honest agents operate at full speed.
